title: Fats Navarro's big sound and Freddie Hubbard
summary: Navarro had a big sound from his mouthpiece and training, and Butler says Freddie Hubbard plays everyone's style, advising to perfect what one is.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: So, you are saying that, so you feel that of the bebop trumpet players, then, you feel that Fats Navarro was more connected to like Armstrong's tradition? Of a lyrical trumpet player, even though he was using a different style?
You told me about his sound too, you said he had the most beautiful sound.
Yes, he did. Well, what he -- he was too young to care too much about Pops. He was himself.
Well, I didn't mean so much he was copying Armstrong.
I just meant that -- the lyrical sound --
Well, probably he was using the mouthpiece that made that big sound, see, and then he had academic training, which made him have to have that big sound. That's what happened, see?
These things happened too, so -- and some people think that that's -- that that funny sound is a sound for the trumpet.
Now, what's this man -- Freddie Her --
Well, see this man is, that man is something else, you see. This man is really something else.
Now, he plays everybody. See. He played that first part, and all them parts, and don't turn him loose because he's a demon. So, there you are.
Whatever he says he says -- I'm going to perfect what I am. You see, a young man is a good man, if you are an old man, be a good old man.
